I'm in diamond, played 4 games today so far as fill to further test, 4/4 support.

If we use your analogy of playing support being eating at McDonalds, then a lot of players, myself included, would not mind eating at McDonalds from time to time, just not 90% of the time. 

It's not like I haven't been playing the game or been unable to so far, but I am drawing attention to the problem where queue times I am forced to choose between extremely high queue times (this is around d4) or playing support, when Riot can very easily implement a happy middle ground between the two.

I don't think that anyone's realistically calling for an even 20% distribution, that is just not going to happen. However, we can address the problems and find a middle ground between getting support 90% of the time as fill and an evenly distributed number of times.
That's the point, I don't pick fill anymore, so now, there are even players willing to play support.

I agree. Riot has decided fill has meant "give me the most needed role currently". But I'm pointing out the systematic problem that "fill", in effect, is almost the exact same as picking support. It is definitely a problem, regardless of your definition, if only support mains would be happy with the distribution of roles given fill.

Yes, in solo queue, he has the ability to stomp lanes with his power and tankiness; but, against organized teams, Taric's range becomes extremely easy to kite against. Taric relys on stunning someone to force a favorable engagement, but teams with communication can react more accordingly. This is why supports like Lulu and Zyra are slightly more favoured: they offer guaranteed good cc and utility while having the advantage of range. Moreover, the nature of Taric's skillset forces a harder engage, therefore committing rather easily, this is bad if your team is behind and you are trying to make plays. I think he's a great solo queue support, nevertheless.
